findings.description: SHEET-FORMULA-002 frames the guarantee as uniform: 'each per-row formula' is written 'as references to that row's own cells.' In the real code, only 5 of the 7 live-formula Positions columns actually contain same-row cell references (Market Value `=E{r}*B{r}`, Unrealized P&L `=F{r}-D{r}`, Est. Unrealized Tax `=G{r}*H{r}`, Net Unrealized `=G{r}*(1-H{r})`, Unrealized % `=IF(D{r}=0,0,G{r}/D{r})`). The other 2 — Price `=GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}","price")` and Quote Date `=IFERROR(TEXT(INT(GOOGLEFINANCE("{ticker}","tradetime"))-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` — contain NO cell reference at all, own-row or otherwise; the resolved ticker (via `config::AliasMap::resolve`) is baked into the formula text as a literal string. Both directions trip on this: all 3 A sketches, working from the EARS text alone, independently guessed the OPPOSITE mechanism — a same-row cell-reference lookup for the ticker (A1: `=GOOGLEFINANCE(A2,"price")`; A2: `=GOOGLEFINANCE(B2)`; A3: `=GOOGLEFINANCE(A2,"price")`) — a converged-but-wrong sub-decision the EARS text invited. All 3 B reconstructions transcribe the real literal-ticker formula text correctly (verbatim match to `lib.rs`), yet then restate the 'references only that row's own cells / no other row's number' rule as if it applies uniformly to every formula column listed (including Price/Quote Date), without ever flagging that those two contain zero row-number references to leak in the first place. Neither direction surfaces the asymmetry cleanly, even though both had the information needed to.

SHEET-FORMULA-002 gives no column schema, so all 3 A sketches invent their own ticker/price column letters (A1: A/D; A2: caller-injected ticker_col/price_col; A3: A/B) and a minimal 2-column layout. Real code fixes a 13-column Positions schema (A Symbol … E Price … H Est. Tax Rate … M Quote Date) via `POSITIONS_HEADER`, defined outside this EARS item. Expected/self-acknowledged invention (each A explicitly flags it as an assumption), not a surprising gap, but it confirms the EARS text alone under-determines layout.

All 3 A sketches scope 'formula generation' as a standalone pure function of `row_count` (plus fixed config constants), decoupled from any source data. Real code's per-row formula construction is inline inside `render_positions`, interleaved with engine-value computation (avg cost/share, tax rate lookup, symbol identity) and driven by `Snapshot` + `effective_rates` + `AliasMap` — never a bare row count. A grain-level mismatch, expected given the A's were implementing only the narrow formula-anchoring clause.

B1/B2/B3 (high mutual agreement, near-verbatim match to the real code) reconstruct substantial content that SHEET-FORMULA-002's text neither states nor implies: the exact formula text for Market Value/Unrealized P&L/Est. Unrealized Tax/Net Unrealized/Unrealized %; the full value-vs-formula column-typing split (6 value / 7 formula columns); the `Est. Tax Rate` percent-string/`userEnteredValue`-coercion contract; the locale-proof Quote Date `IFERROR(TEXT(INT(...)-DATE(1970,1,1),"0"),"")` encoding; and the Tax tab's all-kernel-value (zero-formula) invariant. All of this is pinned by `formula.rs`'s assertions but lives well outside this EARS ID's stated scope (row-anchoring + own-cell-reference + frozen header + anti-mispair) — legitimate 'code enforces more than this EARS states' signal, though it also shows the B reconstructions weren't scoped to the single target ID.

All 3 B outputs fold the `Err(ViewError::DuplicateSymbolRow(symbol))` guard into the 'row identity/pairing' concern of SHEET-FORMULA-002. Per the code's own comment, this guard is a structurally-UNREACHABLE defensive assertion against a same-symbol-twice `Snapshot.positions` map (impossible through the real `Map<Symbol,_>`-typed API) — an invariant about the upstream snapshot's key uniqueness, not about a row shifting after publish (the actual 'row shift cannot mis-pair' scenario the target EARS names). All three B's attribute it to the same requirement regardless, illustrating how an unscoped code-only reconstruction blends an adjacent invariant into the audited concern.

B2 and B3 note the frozen-header contract is enforced by a hard `assert_eq!` panic in `InMemorySheetsView::batch_update_view` (any republish presenting a different header panics unconditionally, 'not via a release-stripped' check, per the source comment) — a specific enforcement mechanism SHEET-FORMULA-002's text is silent on (it states the outcome 'never-rewritten,' not that a violation is caught by a hard panic in test infrastructure).
